target.section: Design > Designer's calls > Service-enforced routes now refuse a keyless caller first

action.newText: Service-enforced deletion routes check action keys before executing the deletion command. For DELETE /projects/:slug/tickets/:ref/links/:linkId, the route gate refuses callers holding neither ticket.link.remove nor ticket.link.remove.own with 403 permissions before any link lookup. For DELETE /comments/:id, resolveCommentProject runs first; missing comments, deleted tickets or projects, and non-members receive 404 comments with no request. After successful resolution, the route gate refuses callers holding neither comment.delete nor comment.delete.own in that project with 403 permissions and no request. Comment row-ownership checks remain in the deletion command.

rationale: Verified CommentsService.assertCommentProjectMembership performs the owning-project lookup and hides membership refusals as 404. ApprovalRouteGate.run checks canHoldKey using the supplied projectId. This correction removes only the contradictory ordering claim, preserving the spec's detailed design and ACs.

action.text: Supersede only the obsolete roster-only fixture requirement. Do not restore AgentProject storage or legacy authorization. Fix, and update acceptance tests: use the agent baseline plus project-scoped bindings granting exactly project.read, comment.create and comment.delete.own, without comment.delete or wildcard grants. In core-comments-labels-watchers.integration.spec.ts AC-9, assert DELETE returns 202, the comment remains pending approval, and root approval executes deletion. Rename the fixture description to binding-based access. Nax must propagate this correction to brief AC-5/spec AC-6 and regenerate any affected managed acceptance material; the implementer must not edit or force-commit nax-owned artifacts. This resolves F6's obsolete fixture requirement, not approval of the whole story.

rationale: Verified the DROP TABLE migration, current RoleBinding schema, project.read-based ProjectAccessService, and comment membership wrapper. A roster-only agent cannot satisfy the required existing authorization path. This narrow correction preserves approval and ownership behavior without changing production auth or reversing a completed migration, and remains consistent with D-1.

action.reason: The deferred minor is a verified correctness defect: vcs-connection.service.ts compares the entire connection, so routine polling can turn a successful connection test into a failed approval despite unchanged target and credentials.

rationale: The spec preserves the service's connection-test result; it does not authorize failures caused by unrelated polling metadata. Fix this narrow regression while retaining conservative target-change detection. Afterward, promotion remains conditional on green CI.

action.reason: The previously identified defect remains at vcs-connection.service.ts:258: whole-connection equality still fails successful tests when routine polling changes metadata.

rationale: The requested correction has not landed. Unrelated polling must not turn a successful provider test into a failed approval. The evidence also explicitly reports that the subsequent CI repair was not re-reviewed.
